o: Break a complex problem into smaller tasks.
Choose which details matter in a computational model.
c: Computational thinking helps define a problem so a computer solution can be designed. OCR J277 specifies abstraction, decomposition and algorithmic thinking.
Split a large problem into manageable subproblems, such as input, calculations, checking and output. Each subproblem can be developed and tested more easily.
Identify essential details and ignore information not needed to solve the problem. A simplified map may show roads and stations but omit the colour of nearby buildings.
First identify the required result; break the job into parts; retain information each part actually needs. Abstraction does not mean deleting important data.

m.title: Model decomposition and abstraction
m.q: A club wants a program to calculate the cost of booking sports courts. Explain how decomposition and abstraction would help create the program. [4 marks]
st: Define the task: calculate and display a booking cost.
Decompose into input duration, get hourly price, calculate total and display it [1], making development manageable [1].
Abstract away irrelevant details such as court wall colour [1], keeping duration and rate needed to calculate cost [1].
Use specific examples from the booking problem.

w: A cinema needs an online ticket-pricing program. Explain two ways decomposition helps the programmer. [4 marks]
Break it into input age/ticket type, calculate prices and output total [1], making each subproblem manageable [1]. Each component can be tested separately [1], helping locate errors [1].
A bus-route planner uses distances and stops but ignores building colours. Explain how abstraction helps. [4 marks]

Abstraction keeps distances and stops needed for route calculation [1], so the model contains relevant features [1]. It ignores building colours [1] because that information does not affect the route [1].
A school lunch app totals several purchases. Explain how decomposition and abstraction work together. [4 marks]

Decomposition splits the task into taking item prices, adding totals and displaying payment [1], simplifying work [1]. Abstraction keeps prices and quantities [1] while ignoring irrelevant details such as a pupil's favourite colour [1].

k.q: Predict the cost of two tickets using a short decomposed calculation.
k.code:
adultPrice = 8
childPrice = 5
total = adultPrice + childPrice
print(total)
p: Add another variable bookingFee = 2 and include it in the total.
k.a:
Original total: 13. Changing childPrice to 6 gives 14.

Extension:
adultPrice = 8
childPrice = 6
bookingFee = 2
total = adultPrice + childPrice + bookingFee
print(total)

Output: 16.
